subject: Thresholded degradation: April 28 maintenance boundary review
messages:
From: Susan Wright <susan.wright@electromed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@electromed.com>
Date: 2026-04-29T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Observed cross-region 5xx during April 28 maintenance window — credit calculation request

Hi Marissa,

We reviewed our incident timeline for Apr 28 and see repeated 5xx responses across multiple regions between 02:12 and 02:28 UTC. Your maintenance advisory listed a maintenance window of 02:10–02:20 with an expectation that impacts outside that window would be considered separately. Because our telemetry shows errors continuing beyond the window (and impacting customer-facing workflows), we're asking Redwood to: 1) confirm the uptime calculation used for this incident, 2) explain any third-party exclusions applied, and 3) provide the proposed credit (if any).

I've attached a short CSV with our error counts and a link to our monitoring dashboard: https://monitor.electromed.com/boards/incident-411.

We'd like a clear apportionment of minutes that count against Redwood's SLA so we can reconcile internally.

Thanks,
Susan Wright
Head of Reliability
ElectroMed Inc.

Attachments: april28_observed_errors.csv (CSV)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Susan Wright <susan.wright@electromed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@electromed.com>
Date: 2026-04-29T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed cross-region 5xx during April 28 maintenance window — credit calculation request

Hi Susan,

Thanks for the data — we've received your CSV and the dashboard link. We're investigating now. Quick notes up front: our published maintenance window was 02:10–02:20 UTC (notice sent Apr 21). Per the SLA, maintenance within the published window is excluded from uptime calculations, but any persistent partial degradation beyond that window may qualify for credits depending on apportionment.

Can you confirm the exact timestamps (to the second) for the first sustained 5xx and the last 5xx you observed? Also attaching the support ticket we've opened for tracking: SUP-12345.

I'll loop our infra lead; Ben and Jonas are on technical analysis and will follow up with probe-level details.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Susan Wright <susan.wright@electromed.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@electromed.com>
Date: 2026-04-29T12:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed cross-region 5xx during April 28 maintenance window — technical findings

On Wed, Apr 29, 2026 at 11:05 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Can you confirm the exact timestamps (to the second) for the first sustained 5xx and the last 5xx you observed?

Hi all,

Quick technical summary from our side: we see a scheduled KV-cache flush task that started at 02:10:12 UTC and completed at 02:19:58 UTC on the control plane. Probe sampling in our edge fleet shows a spike in 5xx beginning at 02:20:05 UTC and subsiding by 02:28:37 UTC. That indicates an overlap where the last bit of cache propagation caused transient errors outside the announced maintenance window.

Important: our policy for apportionment distinguishes between (A) maintenance that was announced and executed within the window and (B) downstream third-party provider outages. In this case, our internal telemetry shows the primary source correlates to cache invalidation propagation and an edge routing flap that resolved within ~8m30s after the window closed.

I've attached a short probe summary that breaks down error counts by region and minute. If ElectroMed's monitoring shows sustained errors beyond 02:28:37 UTC, please share the per-second logs; we can re-open apportionment.

Attachments: probe_summary.pdf (PDF)
Runbook reference: https://drive.redwood.com/maintenance/apportionment-guidelines

Regards,
Ben Carter
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@electromed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Wright <susan.wright@electromed.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-30T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed cross-region 5xx during April 28 maintenance window — technical findings

On Thu, Apr 29, 2026 at 12:38 PM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> our internal telemetry shows the primary source correlates to cache invalidation propagation and an edge routing flap that resolved within ~8m30s after the window closed.

Hi Ben,

Thanks — we pulled per-second logs from our side (attached) and confirm the last observed 5xx at 02:30:12 UTC. That extends ~1m35s beyond your edge flap window. That's significant for several of our SLAs (we count any sustained >60s cross-region error as an incident). We're also seeing increased latency for a further ~3 minutes until 02:33:10 UTC in EU probes.

ElectroMed's position is that a third-party exclusion is acceptable only if the outage is attributable to a distinct provider with separate ownership (e.g., CDN vendor). In this case, the timeline suggests Redwood's cache propagation and routing behavior had primary responsibility.

We propose Redwood use an apportionment method that: 1) counts any minutes with confirmed 5xx across >=2 regions as Redwood-implicated, 2) caps third-party exclusion to explicit vendor incidents with matching vendor tickets. Please advise on the credit calculation you will apply and whether you accept our proposed apportionment for this incident.

Thanks,
Sam Patel
Senior Reliability Engineer
ElectroMed Inc.

Attachments: electromed_persecond_0428.log (LOG)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Susan Wright <susan.wright@electromed.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@electromed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed apportionment and next steps — SUP-12345

Hi Susan and Sam,

Appreciate the detailed logs and patience while we completed our analysis. Summary of findings:
- Published window: 02:10:00–02:20:00 UTC.
- Redwood internal propagation and edge flap metrics indicate primary activity 02:10:12–02:28:37 UTC.
- ElectroMed observed 5xx through 02:30:12 UTC and elevated latency until 02:33:10 UTC in some EU probes.

Proposed resolution:
- We will exclude the announced maintenance minutes (02:10–02:20) per SLA.
- For 02:20:00–02:28:37 (our probe-determined edge flap window) we propose apportioning responsibility to Redwood for 100% of minute-level impact.
- For 02:28:38–02:30:12 (the additional 1m35s ElectroMed observed), we propose a shared apportionment: Redwood 60% / Third-party 40% to account for propagation tail and overlapping vendor routing behavior.
- For latency-only minutes after 02:30:12 through 02:33:10 we propose no uptime credit but an operational follow-up (we will open a postmortem and adjust cache invalidation throttle parameters).

Under that approach, the credit calculation yields a partial credit equal to 0.6 * (minutes counted as downtime outside the maintenance window) applied to the monthly SLA unit. We'll prepare a formal calculation and a DocuSign for an agreement to this apportionment. See draft: https://docusign.com/abc123 and tracking Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-12345.

If you agree to the apportionment above, please reply with "Approve" and we'll route the credit and timeline into billing. If you disagree, let us know which minute blocks you'd reassign.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: april28_telemetry.csv, probe_summary.pdf, support_ticket_SUP-12345.log
